## Summary

**The claim: "4× more of our PRs pass first review"** since running one skill at the end of every coding session. They open-sourced it: **make-native**, MIT, at [github.com/Sloydai/make-native](https://github.com/Sloydai/make-native) (27 stars at capture, pushed 2026-11-05 — hours before the tweet).

**The problem it names precisely:** coding agents (and people in a hurry) add features with least disturbance — an `if (newThing)` here, a flag there, a copied component "just for this case". Each change is safe alone; together the code only makes sense if you know the order it was written in.

**What the skill does** (README-verified): takes the feature diff and asks — *if the original author had known about this feature on day one, what would the code look like?* — then writes that version, deletes the workarounds, rewrites the tests. Concretely: reads the diff against the PR base branch, reads surrounding code/types/callers/git history, redesigns the touched code as if the feature were in the original spec, makes common cases simple, **rewrites tests to match and deletes tests that only preserved the workaround**, and checks no trace of the old workaround remains.

**Smell list it hunts:** aliases re-deriving a value the code already has; `if (newKind)` branches where the code already dispatches on kind; near-copies of an existing file/component for one variant; flags duplicating what a type already says; a second system for a concern that already has one (cost tracking, logging, retries, config).

**Boundary:** features only — "Bug fixes should stay minimal, so don't run it on a bug-fix commit." Output is a separate commit (`refactor` if behavior unchanged, `feat` if not) so the reshape reviews apart from the feature.

**The tweet's image** (OCR'd + cross-validated against the repo's own before-after.png alt text): a bolted-on `save(media, isVideo?)` with a copied `{gif, png}` SAVERS map and separate gifCopy call → rewritten as one more `{gif, mp4, png}` entry in the existing SAVERS table and a plain `save(media)`. The whole thesis in one diff.

**Real example from the README:** run on the "What is Sloyd" page feature — found an optional `locale` prop only 1 of 7 call sites passed (fixed: make it required + route through the existing coverage check; localized links went 1→17 of 28) and the same rule written twice across `/llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` (both now read from the module that already owned the opposite rule; `/llms.txt` came out byte-identical).

**Install:** `npx skills add Sloydai/make-native` — works with Claude Code, Codex, opencode, Kiro, GitHub Copilot. Single-file skill (SKILL.md).

## Why it matters

**The strongest idea here is the review-shaped framing.** "Code that only makes sense if you know the order it was written in" is exactly the debt agent-driven development accumulates fastest — agents optimize for least-disturbance diffs because that's what passes review cheaply. Reframing the fix as *make the feature look native to the codebase* (rather than "clean up later") attacks the debt at commit time, when the context is still loaded. The 4× first-review-pass number is self-reported and unfalsifiable — treat as marketing, not measurement.

**Second-strongest: deleting tests that only preserve the workaround.** Most refactoring guidance leaves test debt untouched; naming test-rewriting as part of the reshape (not an afterthought) is the detail that makes this more than a lint-runnable.

**Skepticism gates:**

- **4× claim is a tweet number** — no baseline, no denominator, no methodology. The mechanism is plausible; the multiplier is not evidence.
- **27 stars, released yesterday** — zero community validation yet; the README example is the authors' own site (dogfooding, which is honest, but n=1).
- **LLM-rewritten code can silently change behavior** while claiming equivalence — the separate-commit discipline mitigates (you review the reshape diff), but "checks that no trace of the old workaround remains" is a heuristic, not a proof.
- Fits an emerging pattern: end-of-session verification/refactor skills as the new CI layer for agent-written code.

**Connection to our stack:** directly relevant to our own coding workflows — every Hermes/Paperclip repo change already goes through the PR + AI review gate; make-native is a candidate pre-review pass on feature branches. Cheap to trial (single-file skill, MIT).
